newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Burton banks on fashion chains.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Burton banks on fashion chains.

text.p: John Hoerner, chief executive of British fashion retailer Burton Group Plc, said on Tuesday that the group's fashion chains had a long way to go before becoming a true growth business but had great potential.

Speaking after Burton announced plans to demerge and seek a separate listing for its Debenham's department stores, Hoerner declined to give details of the growth potential of Burton's remaining "multiples" businesses which include Top Shop and Dorothy Perkins chains.
"Multiples, quite frankly is a good business," he said. "But it has got a long way to go. So I would have to say that it is still a little bit of a recovery business."
But he added: "I wouldn't be doing what I'm doing with the multiples business if I didn't think there was great potential. I'm not volunteering for this as charity work."
Excluding home shopping, Debenham's saw sales jump 9.4 percent in the first half of the year compared to a 5.8 percent rise in the fashion stores' sales.
But Hoerner said that he hoped to see a "real difference" in the performance of the fashion stores business when they begin trading under the new structure next spring.

Having been credited with masterminding Burton's dramatic turnaround from troubles in the British recession of the early 1990s, Hoerner said after working on Debenhams for 10 years it was a world class store.
Asked how long it would take to rev up the group's other businesses, Hoerner said: "I've been working on multiples for five years. I hope it isn't going to take another five."
Burton, which has the second biggest market share in clothing after Marks and Spencer Plc, has successfully rebuilt gross profit margins and revamped its womenswear chains to boost profits.
"I'm going to be working very hard but I'm going to be doing things I love," Hoerner said.
